projects.title: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS 2D String DP)
projects.description: Find length of Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) between strings s1 and s2. 2D DP state `dp[i][j]` stores LCS length of prefixes `s1[0..i-1]` and `s2[0..j-1]`: 1) If `s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]`: `dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]`; 2) Else: `dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])` in `O(M * N)` time! In this project, you will build LCS 2D String DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) 2D DP, Character Match Transitions & Sequence Alignments
projects.exampleText: Find LCS length for s1='abcde' and s2='ace'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Common Subsequence (LCS 2D String DP) ---
LCS Length for 'abcde' and 'ace' = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Character Match**: If `s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]`, increment `1 + dp[i-1][j-1]`.
2. **Mismatch Maximum**: If `s1[i-1] != s2[j-1]`, take `max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lcs()`: Solves Longest Common Subsequence using 2D String DP.

projects.title: Longest Common Substring (Contiguous Substring Match DP)
projects.description: Find length of longest CONTIGUOUS substring common to strings s1 and s2. 2D DP state `dp[i][j]` stores common substring ending at `s1[i-1]` and `s2[j-1]`: 1) If `s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]`: `dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]`; 2) Else: RESET `dp[i][j] = 0`! Solved in `O(M * N)` time. In this project, you will build Longest Common Substring Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Contiguous Substring DP, Mismatch Reset Rule (`dp[i][j] = 0`) & Global Maximum Tracking
projects.exampleText: Find Longest Common Substring for 'abcdgh' and 'abcdfgh'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Common Substring (Contiguous Substring Match DP) ---
Longest Common Substring Length for 'abcdgh' and 'abcdfgh' = 4 ('abcd')
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Match Continuation**: If `s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]`, `dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]`.
2. **Mismatch Reset**: If characters differ, set `dp[i][j] = 0`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `longest_common_substring_demo()`: Solves Longest Common Substring using 2D DP.

projects.title: Edit Distance (Levenshtein Distance Insertion/Deletion/Substitution DP)
projects.description: Find minimum single-character operations (Insert, Delete, Replace) to convert string s1 into s2 (Levenshtein Distance). 2D DP state `dp[i][j]` stores edit distance: 1) If `s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]`: `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]`; 2) Else: `1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1])` in `O(M * N)` time! In this project, you will build Edit Distance Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Levenshtein Edit Distance, 3-Operation Min Reduction (Insert, Delete, Replace) & Spellcheckers
projects.exampleText: Compute edit distance between 'horse' and 'ros'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Edit Distance (Levenshtein Distance 2D DP) ---
Edit Distance between 'horse' and 'ros' = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Operations Choices**: `dp[i-1][j]` (Delete), `dp[i][j-1]` (Insert), `dp[i-1][j-1]` (Replace).
2. **Min Recurrence**: Take `1 + min(Delete, Insert, Replace)` on mismatch.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_distance()`: Solves Edit Distance using 2D DP.

projects.title: Distinct Subsequences
projects.description: Given strings S and T, count total distinct subsequences of S that equal T. 2D DP state `dp[i][j]` stores match count: 1) If `S[i-1] == T[j-1]`: `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + dp[i-1][j]`; 2) Else: `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j]`. Solved in `O(M * N)` time! In this project, you will build Distinct Subsequences Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Subsequence Counting DP, Dual Path State Accumulations & String Target Matching
projects.exampleText: Count distinct subsequences of 'rabbbit' matching 'rabbit'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Distinct Subsequences (String Matching 2D DP) ---
Distinct Subsequences count for 'rabbbit' matching 'rabbit' = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Match Accumulation**: Include matching character (`dp[i-1][j-1]`) PLUS skip matching character in S (`dp[i-1][j]`).
2. **Mismatch Skip**: Take `dp[i-1][j]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `distinct_subsequences_demo()`: Solves Distinct Subsequences using 2D String DP.

projects.title: Shortest Common Supersequence
projects.description: Find shortest string that contains both s1 and s2 as subsequences. Compute LCS table `dp[M][N]`, then backtrack through DP table to construct supersequence string in `O(M * N)` time! Length = `len(s1) + len(s2) - LCS_len`. In this project, you will build Shortest Common Supersequence Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Shortest Common Supersequences, DP Backtracking Construction & Subsequence Invariants
projects.exampleText: Find shortest common supersequence for 'abac' and 'cab'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Shortest Common Supersequence (LCS String Reconstruction) ---
Shortest Common Supersequence for 'abac' and 'cab' = 'cabac'
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **LCS Table**: Build standard LCS 2D DP table.
2. **Backtrack Reconstruction**: Backtrack from `(M, N)`: include matching char once, non-matching chars from both strings.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `shortest_common_supersequence_demo()`: Solves Shortest Common Supersequence via LCS DP backtracking.

projects.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence (LPS Interval DP)
projects.description: Find length of Longest Palindromic Subsequence (LPS) in string S. Interval DP state `dp[i][j]` stores LPS length of substring `S[i..j]`: 1) If `S[i] == S[j]`: `dp[i][j] = 2 + dp[i+1][j-1]`; 2) Else: `max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j-1])` in `O(N^2)` time! In this project, you will build LPS Interval DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Interval Dynamic Programming, Outer Substring Length Loops & Palindromic Subproblems
projects.exampleText: Find LPS length for string 'bbbab'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Palindromic Subsequence (LPS Interval DP) ---
Longest Palindromic Subsequence Length for 'bbbab' = 4 ('bbbb')
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Length Outer Loop**: Loop interval length `len` from 2 to N.
2. **Boundary Match**: If `S[i] == S[j]`, `dp[i][j] = 2 + dp[i+1][j-1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lps_interval_dp_demo()`: Solves Longest Palindromic Subsequence using Interval DP.

projects.title: Longest Palindromic Substring (Expand Around Center / 2D DP)
projects.description: Find longest CONTIGUOUS palindromic substring in string S. 2D DP state `dp[i][j]` is true if substring `S[i..j]` is a palindrome: `dp[i][j] = (S[i] == S[j]) && dp[i+1][j-1]`. Solved in `O(N^2)` time! In this project, you will build Longest Palindromic Substring Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Palindromic Substring Verification, Boolean Interval Tables & Center Expansion Comparison
projects.exampleText: Find longest palindromic substring of 'babad'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Palindromic Substring (2D DP / Expand Center) ---
Longest Palindromic Substring of 'babad' = 'bab'
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Base Cases**: Length 1 is true; length 2 is true if `S[i] == S[i+1]`.
2. **Interval Recurrence**: `dp[i][j] = (S[i] == S[j]) && dp[i+1][j-1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `longest_palindromic_substring_demo()`: Solves Longest Palindromic Substring using 2D DP.

projects.title: Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM Classic Interval DP)
projects.description: Given dimensions of N matrices, find optimal parenthesization that MINIMIZES total scalar multiplications. Interval DP state `dp[i][j]` stores min cost to multiply matrices `i..j`: `dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + p[i-1]*p[k]*p[j])` for all `i <= k < j` in `O(N^3)` time! In this project, you will build MCM Interval DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM), Classic Interval DP Cut Points `k` & Dynamic Matrix Parenthesization
projects.exampleText: Find minimum scalar multiplications for 4 matrix dimensions
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM Classic Interval DP) ---
Minimum Multiplication Operations for 4 Matrices = 4500
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cut Point k Loop**: Test all split positions `k` from `i` to `j-1`.
2. **Scalar Multiplication Cost**: `cost = dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + p[i-1]*p[k]*p[j]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `mcm_interval_dp_demo()`: Solves Matrix Chain Multiplication using Interval DP.

projects.title: Burst Balloons (Interval DP Range Splitting)
projects.description: Given N balloons with numbers `nums`, bursting balloon `i` earns `nums[i-1] * nums[i] * nums[i+1]` coins. Find max coins by bursting all balloons. Think BACKWARDS: choose LAST balloon `k` to burst in interval `i..j`: `dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][k-1] + dp[k+1][j] + nums[i-1]*nums[k]*nums[j+1])` in `O(N^3)` time! In this project, you will build Burst Balloons Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Reverse Process Interval DP, Last Element Cut Point Selection & Max Coin Accumulation
projects.exampleText: Calculate maximum coins by bursting balloons
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Burst Balloons (Interval DP Range Splitting) ---
Maximum Coins collected by bursting balloons = 167
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Last Balloon Cut k**: Assume balloon `k` is the LAST balloon burst in interval `i..j`.
2. **Coins Formula**: `dp[i][k-1] + dp[k+1][j] + nums[i-1]*nums[k]*nums[j+1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `burst_balloons_demo()`: Solves Burst Balloons using Interval DP.

projects.title: Minimum Cost Tree From Leaf Values (Interval DP)
projects.description: Given positive integers array, build a binary tree where leaves correspond to array elements in in-order traversal, and non-leaf node value equals product of largest leaf values in left and right subtrees. Minimize total non-leaf node values using Interval DP in `O(N^3)` time! In this project, you will build Min Cost Tree From Leaves Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Binary Tree In-Order Cut Points, Max Leaf Product Invariants & Subtree Sum Minimization
projects.exampleText: Find minimum non-leaf node sum for leaf array
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Cost Tree From Leaf Values (Interval DP) ---
Minimum Non-Leaf Node Sum = 32
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Subtree Max Leaf**: Precompute `max_leaf[i][j]` for range `i..j`.
2. **Interval Cut k**: `dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + max_leaf[i][k] * max_leaf[k+1][j])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_cost_tree_leaf_demo()`: Solves Minimum Cost Tree From Leaf Values using Interval DP.

projects.title: Wildcard Matching (? and * Pattern DP)
projects.description: Match string S with pattern P containing `?` (matches any single character) and `*` (matches any sequence of characters including empty). 2D DP state `dp[i][j]`: 1) If `P[j-1] == '*'`: `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] || dp[i][j-1]`; 2) Else: `(S[i-1] == P[j-1] || P[j-1] == '?') && dp[i-1][j-1]` in `O(M * N)` time! In this project, you will build Wildcard Matching Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Wildcard Pattern DP, Star Transition Branches (Skip vs Match) & 2D String Matching
projects.exampleText: Verify wildcard pattern matching for 'adceb' and '*a*b'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Wildcard Matching (? and * Pattern DP) ---
Does string 'cb' match pattern '?a': NO
Does string 'adceb' match pattern '*a*b': YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Star Match Rule**: `*` can match empty sequence (`dp[i][j-1]`) OR consume character (`dp[i-1][j]`).
2. **Single Match Rule**: `?` matches any single character.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `wildcard_matching_demo()`: Solves Wildcard Matching using 2D Pattern DP.

projects.title: Regular Expression Matching (. and * Pattern DP)
projects.description: Match string S with regex P containing `.` (any single char) and `*` (zero or more of PRECEDING element). 2D DP state `dp[i][j]`: 1) If `P[j-1] == '*'`: `dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-2] || (match && dp[i-1][j])`; 2) Else: `match && dp[i-1][j-1]` in `O(M * N)` time! In this project, you will build Regex Matching Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Regular Expression Regex DP, Preceding Kleene Star Matching & Complex String States
projects.exampleText: Verify regex pattern matching for 'aab' and 'c*a*b'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Regular Expression Matching (. and * Pattern DP) ---
Does string 'aab' match pattern 'c*a*b': YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Zero Kleene Star**: `dp[i][j-2]` treats `char*` as 0 occurrences.
2. **Multi Kleene Star**: `match && dp[i-1][j]` consumes matching character.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `regex_matching_demo()`: Solves Regular Expression Matching using 2D Regex DP.

projects.title: Interleaving String (Dual Pointer 2D Grid DP)
projects.description: Given strings s1, s2, and s3, determine if s3 is formed by INTERLEAVING s1 and s2 while preserving relative character orders. 2D DP state `dp[i][j]` is true if `s3[0..i+j-1]` is formed by `s1[0..i-1]` and `s2[0..j-1]`: `dp[i][j] = (s1[i-1]==s3[i+j-1] && dp[i-1][j]) || (s2[j-1]==s3[i+j-1] && dp[i][j-1])`. In this project, you will build Interleaving String Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Interleaving String Verifications, Dual Pointer Matrix DP & Prefix Character Matches
projects.exampleText: Check if s3='aadbbcbcac' is interleaving of s1='aabcc' and s2='dbbca'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Interleaving String (Dual Pointer 2D Grid DP) ---
Is s3='aadbbcbcac' interleaving of s1='aabcc' and s2='dbbca': YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **s1 Transition**: If `s1[i-1] == s3[i+j-1]`, transition from `dp[i-1][j]`.
2. **s2 Transition**: If `s2[j-1] == s3[i+j-1]`, transition from `dp[i][j-1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `interleaving_string_demo()`: Solves Interleaving String using 2D Grid DP.

projects.title: Palindrome Partitioning II (Min Cuts for Palindromes)
projects.description: Partition string S into minimal cuts such that every substring is a palindrome. Precompute 2D Palindrome Table `isPalin[i][j]` in `O(N^2)`. 1D DP `minCuts[i]` stores min cuts for `S[0..i]`: `minCuts[i] = min(minCuts[j-1] + 1)` for all `isPalin[j][i] == true` in `O(N^2)` time! In this project, you will build Palindrome Partitioning Min Cuts Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Palindrome Precomputation, 1D Min Cut DP Transitions & Substring Partitioning
projects.exampleText: Find minimum cuts to partition 'aab' into palindromes
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Palindrome Partitioning II (Min Cuts DP) ---
Minimum cuts to partition 'aab' into palindromes = 1 ('aa' | 'b')
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Precompute Palindromes**: Build `isPalin[j][i]` boolean matrix.
2. **1D Cut Recurrence**: `minCuts[i] = min(minCuts[j-1] + 1)` for valid palindrome cuts `j..i`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `palindrome_partitioning_ii_demo()`: Solves Palindrome Partitioning II using 1D/2D DP.

projects.title: Strange Printer (Interval DP Turn Minimization)
projects.description: A strange printer can print a sequence of the same character in 1 turn. Find minimum turns to print string S. Interval DP state `dp[i][j]` stores min turns for `S[i..j]`: 1) `dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1]`; 2) For `k` where `S[k] == S[j]`: `dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][j], dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j-1])` in `O(N^3)` time! In this project, you will build Strange Printer Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Strange Printer Turn Minimization, Character Overprint Invariants & Interval DP Cuts
projects.exampleText: Find minimum turns to print 'aaabbb'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Strange Printer (Interval DP Turn Minimization) ---
Minimum turns to print 'aaabbb' = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Same Character Optimization**: If `S[k] == S[j]`, overprinting character `S[j]` costs 0 extra turns.
2. **Interval Min Recurrence**: Test all matching character cut points `k` in interval `i..j`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `strange_printer_demo()`: Solves Strange Printer problem using Interval DP.

projects.title: Remove Boxes (3D Interval DP Range Collapsing)
projects.description: Given colored boxes, removing K contiguous same-color boxes yields `K * K` points. Find maximum points collected. 3D Interval DP state `dp[i][j][k]` stores max points for `boxes[i..j]` given `k` boxes matching `boxes[i]` attached to its left! Solved in `O(N^4)` time! In this project, you will build Remove Boxes 3D DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 3D Interval DP State `(i, j, k)`, Consecutive Color Accumulation & Range Collapsing
projects.exampleText: Calculate maximum points collected by removing boxes
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Remove Boxes (3D Interval DP Range Collapsing) ---
Maximum points collected by removing boxes = 23
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **3D State**: `k` tracks number of trailing boxes with same color as `boxes[i]`.
2. **2 Choices**: 1) Remove box `i` and `k` attached boxes (`(k+1)^2 + dp[i+1][j][0]`); 2) Merge with matching color box `m` inside `i+1..j`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `remove_boxes_demo()`: Solves Remove Boxes using 3D Interval DP.

projects.title: Minimum Score Triangulation of Polygon (Interval DP)
projects.description: Given N-sided convex polygon with vertex values `values`, triangulate polygon into `N-2` triangles. Score of a triangle is product of its 3 vertex values. Find minimum score triangulation. Interval DP state `dp[i][j]` stores min score to triangulate sub-polygon `i..j`: `dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + val[i]*val[k]*val[j])` in `O(N^3)` time! In this project, you will build Polygon Triangulation Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Polygon Triangulation Geometry, Sub-Polygon Range Cuts & Min Weight Triangulation
projects.exampleText: Calculate minimum score triangulation of convex polygon
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Score Triangulation of Polygon (Interval DP) ---
Minimum Score Triangulation Cost = 13
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Polygon Triangle Cut**: Pick 3rd vertex `k` between `i` and `j` to form triangle `(i, k, j)`.
2. **Cost Formula**: `dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + val[i]*val[k]*val[j]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_score_triangulation_demo()`: Solves Minimum Score Triangulation of Polygon using Interval DP.

projects.title: Travelling Salesperson Problem (Bitmask DP State Compression)
projects.description: Solve TSP (find minimum cost to visit N cities and return to start). Bitmask DP state `dp[mask][u]` stores min cost to visit set of cities in `mask` ending at city `u`. Reduces complexity from brute-force `O(N!)` down to `O(N^2 * 2^N)` time! In this project, you will build TSP Bitmask State Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bitmask State Compression `dp[mask][u]`, Factorial to Exponential Speedup & City Tour Minima
projects.exampleText: Compute minimum TSP tour cost for 4 cities
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Travelling Salesperson Problem (Bitmask DP State Compression) ---
Minimum TSP Tour Cost visiting all 4 cities = 35
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **City Mask**: Bitmask tracks visited cities set.
2. **State Transition**: `dp[mask | (1<<v)][v] = min(dp[mask][u] + dist[u][v])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `tsp_bitmask_dp_demo()`: Solves Travelling Salesperson Problem using Bitmask DP.

projects.title: Number of Ways to Wear Different Hats to Every Person (Bitmask DP)
projects.description: Assign 40 different hats to N people such that every person receives a unique preferred hat. Iterate over hats `1..40` on outer loop and maintain a bitmask `mask` representing people who have received hats in `O(H * 2^N)` time! In this project, you will build Hats Bitmask DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Inverted State Iteration, Bitmask People Sets & Combinatorial Hat Assignments
projects.exampleText: Calculate valid hat assignment combinations
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Number of Ways to Wear Different Hats to Every Person (Bitmask DP) ---
Total valid hat assignment combinations = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Outer Hat Iteration**: Loop hats `1..40` on outer loop.
2. **People Bitmask**: `dp[hat][mask | (1<<p)] += dp[hat-1][mask]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hats_bitmask_dp_demo()`: Solves Number of Ways to Wear Different Hats using Bitmask DP.

projects.title: Smallest Sufficient Team (Bitmask Set Cover DP)
projects.description: Find smallest team of candidates covering all S required skills (Exact Set Cover). Bitmask DP state `dp[mask]` stores minimum candidate list required to cover skill bitmask `mask` in `O(M * 2^S)` time! In this project, you will build Smallest Sufficient Team Bitmask Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bitmask Exact Set Cover, Skill Mask Unions & Minimum Candidate Team Extraction
projects.exampleText: Find smallest candidate team covering all required skills
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Smallest Sufficient Team (Bitmask Set Cover DP) ---
Smallest Team Size covering all required skills = 2 (Candidate IDs: [0, 2])
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Skill Encoding**: Encode skills into bitmask of length S.
2. **Set Cover DP**: `dp[mask | candidate_skills]` stores minimum candidate list.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `smallest_team_bitmask_demo()`: Solves Smallest Sufficient Team using Bitmask Set Cover DP.

projects.title: Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT) Bitwise XOR Convolution
projects.description: Compute bitwise XOR convolutions `C[k] = sum_{i ^ j = k} A[i] * B[j]` for all 2^N bitmask states in `O(N 2^N)` time using the Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT)! In this project, you will build FWHT XOR Convolution Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT), Spectral XOR Convolutions & O(N 2^N) Hadamard Matrices
projects.exampleText: Execute FWHT bitwise XOR convolution over 2^N states
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT) Bitwise Convolution ---
Executed Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform XOR convolution in O(N 2^N) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Hadamard Matrix**: `F(x + y) = F(x) + F(y)` and `F(x - y) = F(x) - F(y)`.
2. **Pointwise Product**: Compute product in Hadamard domain; apply inverse FWHT.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `fwht_dp_convolution_demo()`: Implements Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform XOR convolution.

projects.title: SOS DP (Sum Over Subsets Dynamic Programming) in O(N 2^N)
projects.description: SOS DP (Sum Over Subsets) computes `F[mask] = sum_{sub is submask} A[sub]` for all 2^N bitmask states in optimal `O(N 2^N)` time instead of naive `O(3^N)`. In this project, you will build SOS DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SOS DP (Sum Over Subsets), Dimensional Bit Optimizations & O(N 2^N) Submask Sums
projects.exampleText: Compute Sum Over Subsets for all 2^N bitmask states
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Sum Over Subsets Dynamic Programming (SOS DP) ---
Computed Sum Over Subsets for all 2^N submasks in O(N 2^N) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bit Dimension Loop**: Loop dimension `i` from `0` to `N-1`.
2. **DP Recurrence**: `dp[mask][i] = dp[mask][i-1] + (mask & (1<<i) ? dp[mask ^ (1<<i)][i-1] : 0)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `sos_dp_engine_demo()`: Implements SOS DP (Sum Over Subsets Dynamic Programming).

projects.title: Hirschberg's Linear Space LCS Algorithm in O(M + N) Space
projects.description: Standard LCS string reconstruction requires `O(M * N)` matrix memory. Hirschberg's algorithm combines Divide & Conquer with 1D DP to reconstruct the exact LCS string alignment in `O(M * N)` time and LINEAR `O(M + N)` auxiliary space! In this project, you will build Hirschberg's Linear Space LCS Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Hirschberg's Divide & Conquer LCS, Linear O(M+N) Memory Alignment & Substring Midpoint Splitting
projects.exampleText: Reconstruct exact LCS string in linear O(M+N) space
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Hirschberg's Linear Space LCS Algorithm ---
Computed LCS string alignment in O(M * N) time and linear O(M + N) auxiliary space.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Midpoint Split**: Split s1 at `mid = M / 2`.
2. **Forward/Backward DP**: Compute forward LCS for `s1[0..mid]` and backward LCS for `s1[mid..M]` in 1D space; combine optimal cut point.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hirschberg_lcs_demo()`: Solves Hirschberg's linear space LCS algorithm.

projects.title: Parallel SIMD Vectorized String Edit Distance Matrix Kernel
projects.description: Accelerate String Edit Distance and Levenshtein matrix calculations using 256-bit AVX2 SIMD vector instructions, evaluating 8 character comparisons concurrently in 1 CPU instruction pass! In this project, you will build SIMD Edit Distance Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SIMD AVX2 Edit Distance Vectorization, 256-Bit Parallel Character Match & Hardware Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Evaluate 8 parallel edit distance DP cells in 256-bit AVX2 registers
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Parallel SIMD Vectorized String Edit Distance Matrix Kernel ---
Evaluated 8 parallel character comparison DP cells in 256-bit AVX2 vector registers.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory-Mapped DNA Sequence Alignment DP Kernel
projects.description: Genomic sequence alignment engines (BLAST, Smith-Waterman) align 1,000,000 DNA genomic sequences per second by executing matrix DP kernels directly over memory-mapped shared memory buffers (`mmap`). In this project, you will build Real-Time DNA Sequence Alignment Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory-Mapped DNA DP Buffers, 1M Sequence Alignments & Genomic Smith-Waterman Engine
projects.exampleText: Align 1M genomic DNA sequences per second via memory-mapped DP
projects.exampleOutput:
--- High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time DNA Sequence Alignment DP Kernel ---
Evaluated 1,000,000 genomic DNA sequence alignment DP queries per second.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **mmap Genomic Files**: Map DNA sequence files into RAM virtual address space.
2. **Microsecond Sequence Alignment**: Execute zero-copy Smith-Waterman sequence alignment DP directly from memory offsets.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stream_dna_alignment_demo()`: Simulates high-throughput memory-mapped real-time DNA sequence alignment DP kernel.
